title: Washington Launches a Task Force Against Iran's Land Routes, Saudi Arabia Sounds Civil Defense Alerts in Dhahran, and New Zealand's Election Ends on a Knife-Edge
subhead: US forces widened the eight-month Iran blockade from sea to land by establishing a ground-supply interdiction task force and firing on a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman, even as Saudi civil defense sirens sounded across Dhahran, Dammam, and Abqaiq during Houthi clashes. In the Pacific, New Zealand's general election left parliament separated by a single provisional seat ahead of special vote counts, while Spain's Canary Island of El Hierro declared a state of emergency after 3,300 boat arrivals in the first week of November.

sections.heading: US Expands Iran Blockade to Land Routes and Fires on Cargo Vessel in Gulf of Oman
sections.body:
The United States military announced on Saturday night that it has established a new task force dedicated to disrupting Iran's land-based supply routes used to transport weapons and military materiel across the region, expanding what had previously operated primarily as a maritime interdiction campaign (Al Jazeera, CBS News). At sea, US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed that American forces fired upon and disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after it attempted to breach the naval blockade, while noting that 147 vessels have been redirected since blockade operations tightened (AP News, The Hill, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty).

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported the military incident off Oman as the United Arab Emirates rescued 22 sailors from a stricken vessel in regional waters (Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera). Meanwhile, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz after switching off their navigation transponders on an unauthorized route, and Iranian state media reported blasts heard on Qeshm Island and in the coastal cities of Jask, Sirik, and Bandar Abbas (Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera).

Separately, Tehran announced that it has formally lifted its self-imposed limit on ballistic missile ranges, following statements by IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi that Iranian engineers are actively extending the reach of the country's missile inventory (AP News, Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Pairing a naval blockade with a dedicated land-corridor interdiction task force stretches US surveillance and strike commitments across Iraq and Syria at the exact moment Tehran removes its missile range cap.

sections.heading: Saudi Arabia Activates Warning Sirens Across Eastern Oil Hub Amid Houthi Clashes
sections.body:
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense Directorate activated emergency warning sirens across multiple areas of the kingdom's oil-producing Eastern Province — including Dammam, Al-Ahsa, Abqaiq, and Dhahran, home to Saudi Aramco's headquarters — amid ongoing clashes with Yemen's Houthi movement, before later issuing an all-clear (Times of Israel, Anadolu Agency, Habertürk).

Inside Yemen, the internationally recognized government's armed forces stated they had conducted more than 800 military operations against Houthi positions, killing or incapacitating 130 fighters and destroying or damaging 50 vehicles and missile launchers (Anadolu Agency). At the same time, US Energy Secretary officials stated that a damaged Saudi oil pipeline is expected to return to service within days (EnergyNow).

In Syria, local media reported that Israeli forces entered southern Syrian villages with 14 military vehicles, storming a school and raiding homes, while flash floods near Al-Bukamal in eastern Syria brought down a bridge, killing one person and cutting off several neighborhoods (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Warning sirens in Dhahran and Abqaiq underscore that Saudi energy infrastructure remains under direct aerial threat despite intensive ground operations inside Yemen.

sections.heading: New Zealand Faces Weeks of Coalition Uncertainty After Knife-Edge Vote
sections.body:
New Zealand's general election ended without a clear governing mandate on Saturday night, leaving the country facing weeks of coalition talks while electoral authorities count special and overseas ballots (The Guardian, Times of Israel). Initial counts gave the center-right National Party the largest share of seats in parliament with a razor-thin one-seat provisional lead for the right-leaning bloc, but special votes cast outside home electorates and from abroad — which historically tilt toward left-wing parties — have yet to be tallied (The Guardian, Times of Israel).

With neither major bloc holding a comfortable buffer, a newly emerged centrist party could hold the balance of power once final tallies are certified later this month (Times of Israel). Elsewhere in the Asia-Pacific, a strong earthquake struck central Japan, shattering storefront windows and injuring at least 22 people, while unseasonal spring blizzards brought heavy snow across southeastern Australia in New South Wales, Victoria, and Tasmania (AP News, The Guardian).
sections.whyItMatters: Until special ballots are counted, Wellington cannot finalize a coalition agreement, prolonging policy uncertainty over fiscal spending and defense commitments in the South Pacific.

sections.heading: Poland Declares National Mourning After Kraków Attack as Canary Islands Declare Emergency
sections.body:
Polish President Karol Nawrocki declared two days of national mourning and Prime Minister Donald Tusk labeled Saturday's mass shooting in Kraków an 'act of terrorism' after a gunman dressed in military fatigues opened fire from a car in the city's Main Market Square, killing six people — including a British national — and injuring at least 15 others (BBC, Al Jazeera, The Independent, NBC News). Police later discovered three additional bodies at the attacker's residence, bringing the total death toll linked to the perpetrator to nine (BBC, Star).

In southwestern Europe, authorities on El Hierro, the smallest of Spain's Canary Islands, declared a formal emergency and requested immediate assistance from Madrid after more than 3,300 migrants and refugees arrived by boat since the beginning of November (Al Jazeera). Meanwhile in France, roughly 146,000 demonstrators — including 75,000 in Paris — took to the streets in ongoing protests over living costs and education policy, resulting in 360 arrests (NTV, AFP).
sections.whyItMatters: The discovery of three more victims at the Kraków shooter's home deepens Poland's worst domestic terror investigation in years, while November boat arrivals on El Hierro show Atlantic migration routes accelerating into winter.

sections.heading: Drone Attack Kills Three Colombian Soldiers as Ukraine Endures Overnight Strikes
sections.body:
At least three Colombian soldiers were killed and eight seriously injured in an explosive drone attack on a military base, the Colombian army announced, with additional personnel receiving hospital treatment (AP News, Anadolu Agency). The strike occurred the same week hundreds of American and Colombian troops launched a joint military exercise in Colombia as part of the Pentagon's heightened focus on the Western Hemisphere (Defense News). Elsewhere in South America, a judge in Paraguay ordered preventive detention for impeached former President Santiago Peña following nearly three hours of testimony at the Attorney General's Office over the country's banking crisis (Anadolu Agency, Times of Israel).

In Eastern Europe, Russian drone and missile strikes wounded at least nine people in Ukraine and damaged energy facilities, a bridge, and a kindergarten in the Kyiv region just as Kyiv prepares for upcoming diplomatic talks involving Russia and the United States (AP News, Euronews).
sections.whyItMatters: Armed groups in Colombia are using multi-casualty drone strikes against regular army bases even as US forces train alongside Colombian units on the ground.

bottomLine: Washington widened its campaign against Tehran this weekend by launching a dedicated task force to interdict Iranian land supply corridors while disabling a blockade-running cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. Across the Gulf, Saudi Arabia briefly activated civil defense sirens in Dhahran, Dammam, and Abqaiq amid Houthi clashes, and Iran declared an end to its self-imposed cap on ballistic missile ranges. Outside the Middle East, New Zealand faces weeks of coalition negotiations as special ballots decide a one-seat parliamentary margin, Polish investigators found three more bodies at the home of the Kraków attacker, and a deadly drone strike hit a Colombian army base during a joint exercise with US troops.
sources: AP News, AFP, Al Jazeera, BBC, CBS News, NBC News, The Guardian, Wall Street Journal, The Hill, The Independent, Times of Israel, Euronews, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, Defense News, EnergyNow, UKMTO, Anadolu Agency, NTV, Habertürk
